nativeAudioPreference.label: Native audio preference

autoRetry.label: Retry failed downloads
autoRetry.description: Automatically tries again after a network or server hiccup, waiting longer between each attempt. Downloads blocked by the site are never retried automatically.

autoRemoveCompleted.label: Remove finished downloads
autoRemoveCompleted.description: Takes a download off the Downloads list a few seconds after it finishes. The files stay in your folder; failed and cancelled downloads stay in the list.

concurrentDownloads.label: Downloads at once
concurrentDownloads.description: How many queued items download at the same time. More at once finishes a long queue sooner, but raises the chance a site limits you.

downloadConnections.label: Download connections
downloadConnections.description: Speeds up large downloads by fetching several parts of a video at once. Higher values raise the chance a site limits you.

networkPacing.heading: Gentle downloads
networkPacing.description: Add small waits during each download so Arroxy does not hit the site too aggressively. Values are in seconds.
networkPacing.tooltip: These waits happen inside each download. How many downloads run at the same time is set separately, under Downloads at once.
networkPacing.summary: Waits: {{requests}} between checks, {{downloads}} before media starts, {{subtitles}} before subtitle files.

tooltips.off: Uses only the small baseline pauses Arroxy keeps for media and subtitles.
tooltips.balanced: Default. Adds short pauses between requests and before media starts.
tooltips.careful: Adds longer pauses for large playlists or networks that frequently hit limits.
tooltips.custom: Tune the advanced per-download controls yourself.

closeToTray.toggleDescription: Continue downloads in the background after closing the window.

analytics.toggleDescription: No telemetry. Once a day, an anonymous heartbeat sends the app version, install channel, OS, language and country so we can count active users. No IDs, URLs, video titles or filenames.

cookiesError.heading: Cookies might be the cause

cookiesError.explanationBrowser: Cookies are read directly from the browser. If the browser is currently running, its cookie database may be locked (Chromium-family). The browser must also be signed in to YouTube. Try closing the browser, switching to a different browser, switching to File mode, or turning cookies off.

dpapi.heading: Chrome cookies blocked by Windows encryption
dpapi.explanation: Chrome 127 and newer encrypts cookies in a way other apps can't read on Windows. Try one of the workarounds below.

dpapi.fixFileBody: Export cookies from Chrome with a browser extension, then switch this app to File mode and pick the exported file.
dpapi.fixUnsafeLabel: Launch Chrome with App-Bound Encryption disabled
dpapi.fixUnsafeBody: Add --disable-features=LockProfileCookieDatabase to Chrome's launch shortcut. Warning: this invalidates previously encrypted cookies, so you'll be signed out of every site and need to log in again.

ytdlp.botBlock: Bot protection triggered. The IP you're using is most likely flagged (datacenter range or busy VPN exit). Change your IP or pick a different VPN endpoint and retry. If it keeps failing, this may be a temporary site-side change — Arroxy updates its download engine on launch, so the fix lands automatically once it ships.
ytdlp.ipBlock: Your IP address appears to be blocked. Try again later or use a VPN.
ytdlp.rateLimit: The site is rate-limiting requests from this connection.
ytdlp.ageRestricted: This video is age-restricted and cannot be downloaded without a signed-in account.
ytdlp.unavailable: This video is unavailable — it may be private, deleted, or region-locked.
ytdlp.geoBlocked: This video is not available in your region.
ytdlp.outOfDiskSpace: Not enough disk space. Free up space and retry.
ytdlp.outputNotWritable: Arroxy can't write to the download folder. It may be read-only, on a locked drive, or blocked by your system's privacy settings. Choose another folder or allow access, then retry.
ytdlp.unsupportedUrl: Arroxy doesn't support this URL. Try a link from a different site.
ytdlp.chunkTransferFailure: The server kept cutting the download mid-stream, and Arroxy gave up after retrying. This usually hits the largest video formats (4K HDR / high-bitrate VP9). Retry, switch network/VPN, or pick a lower-resolution format.
ytdlp.missingDependency: Arroxy could not find FFmpeg or FFprobe. Run setup again or set an FFmpeg location, then retry the download.
ytdlp.postprocessFailure: The download finished, but post-processing (merge / mux / convert) failed. Often this is a transient ffmpeg issue — retry, and if it persists try a different format combination.
ytdlp.parse: Couldn't parse the response from the site. The site may have changed how it serves videos. Arroxy updates its download engine on launch — retry in a few minutes once the fix ships.
ytdlp.network: Network error. Check your connection and retry.
ytdlp.drmProtected: This video is DRM-protected. Arroxy can't remove DRM, so the file can't be downloaded.
ytdlp.loginRequired: This video needs a signed-in account.
ytdlp.unknown: Download failed. See the raw output below.

error.forbidden-char: Remove characters that aren't allowed in filenames: \ : * ? " < > |
error.no-unique-token: Add {title} or {id} to the filename so each download gets its own name.
error.empty-segment: Remove the extra / — every folder needs a name.
error.invalid-segment: That folder name isn't allowed. Avoid . and .. and reserved names like CON.
error.resolution-in-dir: {resolution} can't name a folder — the quality isn't known until the download starts.

notice.title: Browse the web right inside Arroxy
notice.body: Find a video on YouTube or any other site and download it from here — no copying links. Sign in to a site here to download videos that need an account.
notice.riskTitle: Sign in with a secondary account
notice.riskBody: Sites like YouTube may flag — and sometimes ban — accounts used with download tools like Arroxy. Use an account you can afford to lose, not your main one.

nudge.off: Cookies are off, so downloads don't use your Explore sign-in.
nudge.file: Downloads use your cookies file, not your Explore sign-in.
nudge.browser: Downloads use your browser's cookies, not your Explore sign-in.

linkCallout.title: Right-click a link to download it
linkCallout.body: Right-click any video, playlist or channel link on the page to download it with your active profile, pick another profile, or open the step-by-step flow.

toolbar.addressPlaceholder: Search {{engine}} or open any site (Vimeo, Instagram…)
toolbar.interactiveHint: Interactive Download: choose format, subtitles and more…
toolbar.grabUnavailable: Open a video, playlist, or channel to download it

adBlock.off: Ad blocker: off — click to turn on
adBlock.starting: Ad blocker: starting — click to turn off
adBlock.on: Ad blocker: on — click to turn off
adBlock.unavailable: Ad blocker: unavailable, its filter lists couldn't be downloaded — click to turn off
adBlock.accountNote: YouTube may push back on ad blockers for signed-in accounts.

settings.title: Explore
settings.description: Browse YouTube or any other site inside Arroxy, and sign in for videos that need an account.
settings.showTabDescription: Turning it off also stops downloads from using your Explore sign-in.
settings.idleUnloadDescription: After 5 minutes on another tab, closes the YouTube home or search page. Coming back reloads it, which takes a few seconds.
settings.searchEngineDescription: Where text typed in the address bar is searched. Links open as typed.
settings.signOutDescription: Clears your sign-ins and browsing data in Explore, on every site.
settings.signOutConfirmBody: This clears your sign-ins and browsing data in Explore, on every site. Downloads that need an account will fail until you sign in again.

error.proxyTitle: Explore can't connect through your proxy
error.proxyBody: Check the proxy in Settings, then try again.
error.loadBody: Check your connection, then try again.

description.auto: The picked streams decide the file type.
description.mp4: Plays almost everywhere. VP9 in an MP4 won't play video in QuickTime.
description.mkv: Holds any codec. Some TVs and phones can't open it.
description.webm: Open format for browsers. Holds only VP9 or AV1 with Opus.

fileType.webmBlocked: WebM can't hold {{codec}}. Choose MKV or MP4.
fileType.smartTvNoWebm: WebM isn't offered with Smart TV: it can't hold H.264.
fileType.mp4CaveatVp9: VP9 in an MP4 won't play video in QuickTime. H.264 plays everywhere.
fileType.mp4CaveatAv1: AV1 in an MP4 needs a recent Mac to play in QuickTime. H.264 plays everywhere.

sitePreference.label: Streams the site does not mark down
sitePreference.reason: skips damaged, watermarked and fallback copies

original.label: Original streams, not AI-upscaled ones
original.reason: an upscaled copy is taller but adds no real detail

size.label: Larger file
size.reason: more detail at the same settings

aiUpscaled.label: AI-upscaled streams
aiUpscaled.description: YouTube offers some old videos in sizes it made with AI. Skip keeps the original streams; you can still pick an upscaled one by hand.

hdrPreference.label: HDR video
hdrPreference.description: Auto picks HDR when this screen can show it, otherwise SDR. HDR looks washed out on regular screens.
